newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Rabo, Robeco try to clear U.S. legal hurdle.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Rabo, Robeco try to clear U.S. legal hurdle.

text.p: Dutch co-operative bank Rabobank Nederland and fund management group Robeco said on Wednesday they were holding talks with the Federal Reserve Board to resolve legal problems in the United States.
The problems with U.S. banking laws have delayed the first stage of unlisted Rabobank's 1.3 billion guilder takeover of the Robeco group, which was to have been completed by now.

Spokesmen for both groups confirmed a Dutch newspaper report that the U.S. Bank Holding Act prevented Rabobank from bringing Robeco's property fund Rodamco under its banking operations in the United States.
But they denied a report in Het Financieele Dagblad that Rabobank would have to forfeit its U.S. banking licence or sell Rodamco's five billion guilder U.S. property portfolio.
Robobank spokesman Jan Dost said the two groups were not facing such a dilemma.
"Neither giving up the banking licence nor giving up the activities of Rodamco in the U.S. at the moment is an option that we are considering," he told Reuters.
"We think we have found a solution through which we can continue both activities," he added, but declined to specify the remedy.
Robeco spokesman Hans de Klerk also said a solution had been found but declined to elaborate on it.
"That will be discussed with the Fed. We have a good hope that it will end in an acceptable result," he said.

Rabobank, the third largest Dutch bank, is paying 500 million guilders for half of Robecam, the Robeco group's management company, and has the option of paying another 500 million guilders to move to full ownership within four years.
Payments to shareholders in the unlisted Robecam bring the total price up to almost 1.3 billion guilders.
Robecam manages the listed Robeco funds and other products.
Dost said the legal problem was the reason the takeover had been delayed.
